title: Fish and Chips
subtitle: Beer-battered cod with thick-cut chips
excerpt: Cod fillets in a crisp, airy beer batter, deep-fried alongside thick-cut chips until both are golden. The British national dish, made properly at home.

recipe.sourceNotes: Fish and chips as a pairing became widespread in Britain in the second half of the 19th century, with the first chip shops (chippies) appearing in the 1860s. The combination of fried fish (brought by Sephardic Jewish immigrants from Portugal and Spain) and fried potato chips (arriving from France or Ireland) became the most popular takeaway food in Britain for most of the 20th century. The beer batter, made with fizzy beer or sparkling water, produces a lighter, crisper coating than a plain flour batter because the carbonation creates bubbles as it fries.

recipeTools.notes: A deep, heavy pan for frying. Or a deep-fat fryer.
For oil temperature: 190 C for the fish, 160 C first fry for chips.

content.text: Double-fry the chips: a first fry at lower heat cooks them through; a second fry at higher heat crisps the outside. Make the batter just before you need it: it should be used cold and the fizz should still be active. Pat the fish completely dry before battering: any moisture prevents the batter from adhering. Fry the chips first and keep warm in a low oven while you fry the fish.

items.preparation: floury variety, peeled, cut into thick chips
for the batter, plus extra for dusting

content.text: Heat the oil in a deep, heavy pan to 160 C. Pat the cut chips dry. Fry in batches for 5 to 6 minutes until cooked through but not coloured. Remove and drain. Set aside. Increase the oil temperature to 190 C.

Make the batter: whisk the flour, cornflour, baking powder, and 1 teaspoon of salt together. Add the cold lager and whisk until just combined. A few lumps are fine. The batter should coat the back of a spoon.
Return the chips to the oil at 190 C and fry for 3 to 4 minutes until golden and crisp. Remove, drain, season with salt. Keep warm in a low oven.

Pat the fish fillets completely dry. Dust with flour. Dip in the batter, let excess drip off, then lower carefully into the 190 C oil. Fry 2 fillets at a time for 5 to 6 minutes until the batter is golden and crisp and the fish is cooked through. Drain briefly. Serve immediately with the chips, malt vinegar, and tartare sauce.
